items.title: US midterms: early results arrive after strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island on the eve of the vote
items.summary: Live pages from CBC and CNBC say polls closed on 3 November with control of the House and Senate in the balance, and Democrats had won the first Senate race reported. CBS and Foreign Policy report US air strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, which US officials called defensive. Trump told the Financial Times he has no immediate plans for renewed strikes, and Iran's foreign minister said mediated talks were proceeding intensively. No final outcome was available at search time, so everything here is provisional.
items.why: US political control and Gulf tension drive oil and market sentiment, which shape corporate budgets and hiring.
items.src: CBS News, CNBC, CBC, Foreign Policy

items.title: Hungary is not blocking Ukraine's EU accession, Kyiv's envoy says
items.summary: Euronews reported the statement from Ukraine's envoy. It comes from a single headline in the search results, so treat it as provisional.
items.why: EU enlargement decisions affect where European firms expand and hire.

items.title: Rupee holds near 94.90 per dollar as RBI measures support it
items.summary: TradingView, about a day old, says the rupee firmed to roughly 94.90 per dollar helped by an RBI special FX window for state oil refiners and its FCNR(B) deposit scheme. A CNBC piece from 16 October quotes analysts expecting pressure into March 2027, with a possible slide toward 100. Nothing dated 4 November turned up, so these are the latest available figures.
items.why: A weak rupee raises import and overseas-education costs and squeezes company margins.

items.title: Sensex jumps 1,225 points to 76,918 and Nifty reclaims 23,800 on 3 November, a fourth straight gain
items.summary: Business Standard reports the Nifty 50 up 1.58% at 23,810.85 and the Sensex up 1.62% at 76,917.85, both at two-month highs and up about 5% over four sessions. Earnings and lower crude are credited, and FMCG led with about 3%. BusinessToday's intraday check had slightly different levels, so figures are provisional.
items.why: Rising markets lift recruiters' risk appetite and campus-hiring plans.

items.title: IT, metals and pharma lagged the 3 November rally
items.summary: Market reports say banks, financials, FMCG, autos, cement and realty led, while IT, metals and pharma traded lower and investors moved away from global AI-linked trades.
items.why: Sector rotation shows which industries may hire more or less aggressively.

items.title: OpenAI merges ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs and plans to push for AI 'speed limits'
items.summary: A tech-news listing says OpenAI is merging the Chat and Work tabs, and plans to lobby for speed limits on the most powerful models when Congress returns on 9 November. It also reports OpenAI hired a former Army Secretary for a national security role. The text was cut off in places, so details are provisional.
items.why: Product and policy moves shape which AI tools employers adopt and how they are regulated.

items.title: Google reportedly curbs AI in school accounts after backlash
items.summary: Search results say Google had told schools that switching off its AI tools would also remove Search access, drew criticism, and the Wall Street Journal later reported it curbed AI in school accounts. No exact date was given, so this is provisional.
items.why: A case study in platform bundling, trust and how brands handle backlash.

items.title: Apple Intelligence reportedly starts testing in China with Alibaba's Qwen on Wednesday
items.summary: One source says Apple starts testing Apple Intelligence in China using Alibaba's Qwen model on Wednesday. It is not confirmed by a primary source.
items.why: Shows how global brands adapt products through local partners in regulated markets.
